record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Let rho(n) be the limiting minimum density of 1s in binary nth-power-free words and extend rho to real exponents x via binary words avoiding factors of exponent at least x. Does rho have discontinuities other than the known right-discontinuities at 7/3 and the integers n >= 3, and is rho piecewise constant?

evidence.quote: Does rho has other discontinuity? What are they? Is rho piecewise constant?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite or infinite word w over the alphabet {0,1}, the exponent of a nonempty factor u of w is defined as |u|/p, where p is the smallest period of u (so a factor of exponent ≥ n is exactly an n-th power for integer n, and more generally factors of fractional exponent are considered for real exponents). For a real number x ≥ 2, call an infinite binary word x-power-free if it contains no factor of exponent ≥ x. Define the density of 1s in a finite binary word as the number of occurrences of the letter 1 divided by the length of the word, and define the lower density of 1s in an infinite binary word w as the liminf over n → ∞ of the density of 1s in the length-n prefix of w. Let
   ρ(x) = inf { lower density of 1s in w : w is an infinite x-power-free binary word },
defined for all real x ≥ 2 for which x-power-free infinite binary words exist (in particular for x ≥ 2 since binary 2⁺-power-free words such as the Thue–Morse word exist; ρ is also defined at integer values n ≥ 3 via n-th-power-free words). It is known that ρ has right-discontinuities at x = 7/3 and at every integer n ≥ 3.

(a) Determine whether ρ has any discontinuities other than these known right-discontinuities at 7/3 and at the integers n ≥ 3, and if so describe them.

(b) Decide whether ρ is piecewise constant on its domain.
artifact.status_search_result: The minimal-density function ρ for power-free binary words has been studied since the 1990s (Berstel; Ochem and others), and discontinuities at 7/3 and at integers n ≥ 3 are known. Recent work (e.g., on low-complexity binary words avoiding (5/2)⁺-powers) refines values of ρ at specific exponents but no source found establishes a complete description of all discontinuities of ρ or proves/disproves piecewise constancy. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On repetition-free binary words of minimal density
status_evidence.snippet: Studies minimal proportion of one letter in x-th power-free binary words as a function of x and proves the function is discontinuous.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes that ρ has discontinuities, including at 7/3, but does not classify all discontinuities.

status_evidence.title: Low complexity binary words avoiding (5/2)+-powers
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on α-power-free binary words with α ≤ 7/3 leaves open questions about ρ.
status_evidence.claim: Recent investigations refine values of ρ at specific exponents but do not resolve the discontinuity/piecewise-constancy question.
